#: unbound collector: two text documents from the control socket, each classified whole — a line protocol has no leaves for a dotted path to name (DESIGN 20), so `whole` is the only regime that can answer for them.
#nothing: Both documents are the daemon reporting on ITSELF, and that is the whole reason this classification is `nothing` rather than a shrug. `status` prints the release, the verbosity and thread counts, the module chain, the process uptime, the compiled-in option words and the pid — every one of them either a build constant identical on every install of the same package, a number this process happens to hold right now, or unbound's own vocabulary. `stats_noreset` is counters and averages: how many queries were answered, how many from cache, how long recursion took. None of it correlates one machine across two captures, none of it says where anything sits, and none of it is a word an operator chose.
#bound: THE BOUND IS STATED because it is a decision and not a shape. Two things would move these entries rather than survive them, and both are configurations this capture does not have. A host that answers its control socket over TCP prints the addresses it listens on, which is location. And `stats_noreset` grows per-zone and per-thread sections when extended statistics or auth zones are configured — a zone name is a name somebody chose, which is content, and the free-text pass is where such a document belongs. A capture carrying either needs its own entry here, written with the document in front of whoever writes it.
#pid: The pid on the last status line is deliberately not treated as identity. It names a process on one boot of one machine and is reassigned every restart, so it correlates nothing across captures — which is the test the word `identity` actually sets. It is also the payload's only free-standing number outside the counters, and substituting it would teach a reader that a pid is a thing this corpus hides.
